chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Sitting cross-legged in the Masjid is the encirclement of the Arabs.'

key_terms.الِاحْتِبَاءُ: Sitting cross-legged or folding the legs in a specific posture
key_terms.حِيطَانُ: Encirclement, surrounding, or characteristic manner (from حيط)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling or significance of sitting cross-legged (ihbā) in the mosque?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith identifies 'al-ihbā' (sitting with legs folded or tucked to the side) as a distinctive cultural marker of the Arabs within the mosque, reflecting the pre-Islamic and early Islamic social etiquette. Scholars note that while the posture itself is neutral, the hadith serves to contextualize the Prophet’s teachings on modesty and decorum, distinguishing between mere cultural habits and acts of worship. It underscores the importance of maintaining a dignified presence in sacred spaces, aligning physical posture with spiritual reverence.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Sitting cross-legged in the Masjid is the encirclement of the Arabs (sitting in a circle)’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from al- Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Sitting in the Mosque in al- ‘Ihtiba ’ posture (knees folded with thighs against the belly by a piece of cloth or by one’s arms) is the wall of Arabs.’”
